story.title: Apple Says More Than 100,000 Apps Optimized for iPhone Duo, Here's What's Still Missing - MacRumors

facts.text: The figure came from Apple itself, and CNET carried the statement from Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations.

She said, “Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day.” That is the whole quantitative claim.
Apple gave no exact count beyond the round number, and this analysis treats it that way.
The announcement is dated November 6, 2026, and it gives developers, buyers and rival phone makers their first hard marker for how fast the new form factor is filling out with software.
The milestone arrives while shoppers are still asking whether the device is worth waiting for.
Our earlier report on iPhone Duo delivery quotes slipping to Jan.
That is a 14-day window in which developers had to get hardware or simulators, rebuild against a new SDK, test two display configurations and push updates through App Review.
Apple faces a similar problem but holds a different set of tools.
It controls the SDK, the review process and the storefront, and it can tell developers exactly which build version qualifies.
The company also has a record of coaxing app support for new device classes, from the original iPad in 2010 to later screen-size changes on the iPhone.
The 100,000 figure in two weeks fits that pattern of coordinated platform pushes.
Several questions have no public answer today.
It has not shared iPhone Duo pricing in the milestone statement, nor sales, specifications beyond what outlets described, or a roadmap for further SDK changes.
Anyone presenting those details as settled is going beyond the record.
According to reports, optimized apps support the full width of the inner and outer displays and place vertical controls in the status bar.
The sections below do exactly that with the apps Apple listed.
Apple appears to have asked developers to target the device before and during release, and it is counting only apps built with the newer SDK.
Lessons from the Duo’s two-display behavior can inform future products, and developers who now understand posture-aware layouts will carry that skill forward.
A studio that skipped Android foldables might still adapt for the Duo because Apple customers tend to spend heavily on apps and because the company will likely feature early adopters.
Rumors about the next Pro iPhone, including the under-display Face ID reports for the iPhone 18 Pro , show Apple working on several screen changes at once.

Apple today announced that more than 100,000 apps have been optimized for the iPhone Duo, released two weeks ago.
It's been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we're grateful for their creativity and innovation.
iPhone Duo app optimization has been a hotly debated topic on social media platforms, with some people pointing out apps that are not yet optimized and others saying the issue is overblown.
More apps are being updated by the day, though, so the situation is improving rapidly.
